summary:
The video opens with the creator establishing her Pinterest credentials and journey. She started Pinterest immediately when starting her blog, and within 3 years was making five figures a month from the blog, and within 4 years was making six figures a month — attributing this success to Pinterest. She has now shifted focus from her blog to her business called The Daily, which came from the blog, so she has experience with both blogging/social media Pinterest and business Pinterest.

The first tip is that the clearer your niche on Pinterest, the faster it grows. The creator recommends having a specific niche like dogs rather than a broad one like animals, because Pinterest will recognize the account as strictly about dogs and show that content when someone searches for dogs. A broad account showing pigs, cows, cats, and dogs won't grow as fast.

The second and described as biggest tip is to focus on SEO on your Pinterest account as much as on your website and blog — literally everything on Pinterest can be SEOed. The creator goes into detail on this in her Pinterest course. The third tip is to use a mix of content designed specifically for Pinterest (created in Canva) plus repurposed content from other platforms like TikTok videos. Pinterest goes through waves of featuring traditional pins versus videos, so having both types covers you through algorithm changes.

Regarding algorithm changes, after 6 years on Pinterest the creator has experienced many. She advises not freaking out when stats drop — wait about a week because 90% of the time stats come back up. If they stay down, change only one thing and evaluate for about 3 weeks, even though Pinterest typically takes 3 months to fully implement changes. Changing your entire strategy at once prevents you from knowing what's working.

The creator shares that when fully focused on her blogging Pinterest, monthly impressions were always over 10 million. Even after significantly reducing pinning, page views have barely changed — still hundreds of thousands monthly from Pinterest, demonstrating Pinterest's lasting value. She emphasizes Pinterest is unique because it's the only social media where people actually click through to websites — she personally rarely clicks out of Instagram but constantly clicks to websites from Pinterest.

The final tip is consistent pinning. When active, the creator pinned every single day as a non-negotiable, using a scheduler. For those with limited time, she advises that if you can only do 5 pins a week, do exactly 5 pins every week rather than inconsistent amounts like 5 one week, 1 the next, 3 after that. The goal is smooth consistency rather than a roller coaster pattern. She mentions her Pinterest course called Perfecting Pinterest covers detailed strategies for both blog and business Pinterest.
